open_points.subject: M02 Slot / author contract action
open_points.text: "slot_id: a stable name the creating agent chooses; unique in the kernel, and a name already taken is refused;" + "created when an agent with the author right issues the first contract version under a new slot name"
open_points.question: When authoring a contract with an existing slot_id, is that valid as a new contract version for that slot, or refused because the name is already taken?
options: Existing slot_id is valid and creates a new ContractVersion under that slot
Any request using an existing slot_id is refused
Existing slot_id is valid only when content matches current contract version
open_points.default_guess: Existing slot_id is valid and creates a new ContractVersion under that slot.

open_points.subject: M02 Slot purpose across later contract versions
open_points.text: "purpose: plain words ... fixed when the slot is created — taken from the request that issues its first contract version"
open_points.question: For later contract-version requests on an existing slot, must `purpose` be omitted, repeated identically, or can it differ (and be ignored/refused)?
options: Require purpose only on first version; omit later
Allow later requests to include purpose but require exact match
Refuse any later request that includes purpose
open_points.default_guess: Require purpose only on first version; if provided later, require exact match.

open_points.subject: M12 Flow purpose across later flow versions
open_points.text: "purpose of a flow is fixed when the flow is created — taken from the request that composes its first version"
open_points.question: For composing additional versions of an existing flow, what is the rule for `purpose` in the request?
options: Required only on first version; omitted later
Allowed later but must match fixed purpose
open_points.default_guess: Allowed later only if it matches the fixed purpose.

open_points.subject: Random-minted identifiers (M07/M11/M19/M24/M25)
open_points.text: "trial_execution_id: minted at random", "binding_id: minted at random", "run_id: minted at random", "approval_id: minted at random", "grant_id: minted at random"
open_points.question: What must the kernel do if a newly minted random id collides with an existing record id?
options: Overwrite existing record (not plausible but unspecified)

open_points.subject: M10 ManifestOperation with no selected service instance
open_points.text: "base_url: the manifest's base URL of the one instance the installation selects for the service" + "service_instances: at most one selected instance per service ... a service with none selected is not invocable" + only `required_headers`/`instance_class` explicitly say they are absent when no instance is selected
open_points.question: If no instance is selected for a service, does a ManifestOperation still exist for propose/accept/proof reads, and is `base_url` absent or is manifest reading refused?
options: ManifestOperation still readable; `base_url` absent; invocation refused
ManifestOperation read is refused when no instance selected
ManifestOperation readable with service-level data only; invocation refused until selection
open_points.default_guess: ManifestOperation remains readable for metadata checks, with `base_url` absent, and invocation is refused.
